analysis: Compared all BASE and HEAD lines of provider-swift/Tests/DarkbloomCLITests/SandboxWorkDiskTests.swift. The nine changes (HEAD lines 197, 226, 246, 279, 304, 334, 375, 402, 426) inject waitlist: .approved into test-only SandboxSetupFlow calls. Existing assertions remain intact for ownership checks, foreground-terminal requirements, installer compatibility/refusal, disk argument forwarding, owner confirmation and post-command rechecks. No concrete security regression is established by these fixture changes; they do not themselves change production execution, attestation, encryption, cache isolation or billing. Relevant contracts are the installer/owner boundary (TB-013, T-061, A-019) and availability (A-018); the supplied T-041 cache-storage protections are not modified here. Integration must inspect the new waitlist dependency and production SandboxSetupFlow ordering: confirm approval cannot be supplied through untrusted runtime inputs, determine whether denial/error stops installer execution and ownership changes, and verify separate tests exercise pending/denied/error states. Those implementations and tests are outside this supplied scope, so approval injection here is not proof of either a production bypass or a correctly enforced gate.
